title.narrative: USAID- Supporting the return of the displaced population in the Ninewa Plains and West Ninewa

description.narrative: (Iraq): U.S. assistance will be used to enable the rapid and sustainable return of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) to their areas of origin, focused in particular on one of the most vulnerable categories of displaced persons in Iraq - survivors of genocide from Kocho and other areas in Sinjar seeking to access durable solutions to rebuild their lives. Assistance, delivered in partnership with the community itself will include tailored shelter services; memorialization efforts; and measures to address other needs as required to allow families to feel safe, and supported in their recovery. Prior to implementing changes in scopes of work to existing programs or starting new awards, all work will be de-conflicted with DRL to avoid duplication of effort and to encourage complementarity of efforts. In addition, U.S. assistance will be used across Iraq to support efforts to prevent radicalization and violent extremism, including piloting the plans of action envisioned in Iraq's National Strategy to Combat Violent Extremism in key locations, such as areas impacted by rural-urban migration due to conflict, rural underdevelopment, and environmental issues. To support both durable solutions and prevention of radicalization and violent extremism, U.S. assistance will also provide access to finance, enhanced employability, and business support aimed at sustainable job creation. 100% of the funding for this activity is attributable to the People-to-People Conflict Prevention and Peacebuilding, Atrocities Prevention, Countering Violent Extremism directives, and $1.5m is attributed to Religious and Ethnic Minorities directive..
